newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Total's US treasurer says options open.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Total's US treasurer says options open.

text.p: Total Petroleum (North America) Ltd (TOPNA) is working hard to improve margins, particularly at its ailing U.S. refineries, while leaving open the option to sell, merge or form a joint venture, said Douglas Kerner, the company's treasurer.
"This company has an ambitious internal improvement program in place and is diligently working to improve earnings," he said in a telephone interview from TOPNA's Denver head office.

"Everything is on the table," said Kerner. "Everyone (in the North American refining business) is talking about doing JVs (joint ventures). We are reviewing all alternatives to maximise shareholder value."

Kerner suggested that TOPNA is more interested in developing its retailing assets than its refining interests. "We've got a very profitable marketing business but our refinery business is not performing well financially," he said. Overall, the company has had small losses for the last two years, primarily because of poor margins for the refineries.

In an effort to improve margins, two of the company's three plants -- a 68,000 barrels per day unit in Ardmore, Oklahoma and a 45,600 bpd unit at Alma, Michigan -- are shifting to higher-margin products.

They will make more specialty solvents, polymer-modified asphalt and aviation fuel and less diesel and gasoline, Kerner said. The small 28,000 bpd plant near Denver is of a simpler construction and is not included in these plans.

However, though TOPNA has a 1997 goal of $80 million in capital expenditure, up from $52 million last year, "we're not talking about investing much in capital dollars" in the refineries, Kerner said, adding that the company's capital spending target is subject to generating that much in cash flow.

Meanwhile, the company's poor performance overall has held back TOPNA's plans to grow its marketing business, which consists of 560 company-operated retail gas stations and 1,500 stores in Colorado, Kansas, Oklahoma and Michigan.
"We have announced a goal to grow about 100 stores...but because the cash flow was not sufficient we've backed away from that...unless there is an attractive acquisition we want," Kerner said.
"But those assets have become quite valuable and expensive," he added.
